lead: Tools and workshop equipment a person owns, from power tools on a battery platform and hand tools to workshop machines, measuring gear, welding, ladders, storage and protective equipment, organised by kind of work and then by tool.

depts.note: Most owners buy into one battery platform, then pick tools within it.

b.m: How hard it works under load
b.v: torque, drilling and driving speed
b.w: Tests weigh this first (Consumer Reports power score; CHOICE gives drilling and torque 30 percent each).

b.v: weight and balance with the battery fitted
b.w: CHOICE gives handling 40 percent.

b.v: higher amp-hours and a wider range of tools on the same battery
b.w: Most people buy into one battery platform, then choose tools within it.

b.v: battery life over many charges; kick-back cut-off
b.w: Tested separately from power.

b.v: brushless beats brushed
b.w: Checked after the measured results.
Only a rough guide to power (Consumer Reports).

s.brief: Make the cordless battery platform the organising archetype: Tool battery kind with one archetype per platform (DeWalt 20V MAX / 18V XR and FlexVolt, Milwaukee M18 and M12, Makita 18V LXT, 40V XGT and 12V CXT, Ryobi ONE+, Bosch Professional 18V / Power for All / AMPShare, Festool 18V, Metabo CAS, Hilti Nuron, Einhell Power X-Change, Ridgid, Ego for garden crossover). Versions = generations/cell formats (e.g. tabless/pouch packs). Detail = Ah and voltage. Charger merged with its platform as a type, not a SKU list. Remove platform ranges repeated across power-tool kinds (they live here and in the brand register).

k.brief: Archetypes = platforms; source each from maker or Wikipedia page.
Types: standard, rapid, multi-bay; cut Makita SKU list to one line per platform.

s.brief: Restraint: trim SKU lists to market-covering makers plus Which?/CHOICE/Consumer Reports winners (≈5–8). Drop repeated platform ranges (now in Battery platforms). Magnetic drill stays kind-level with no models (trade). Demolition hammer moves here from the old breakers shelf.
Restraint: trim mitre-saw and circular-saw SKU lists; sliding/compound as types; wall chaser and cut-off saw join from the old breakers shelf, kind-level.
Restraint: trim models; keep distinct sander kinds; drywall sander kind-level.

Enthusiast end: Festool Domino as the originating archetype of the new loose-tenon joiner kind (DF 500, DF 700 versions), Lamello as the biscuit-joiner originator, Dremel as the rotary-tool originator (Moto-Tool era, 3000/4000/8220 versions), Fein MultiMaster as the oscillating multi-tool originator, Makita RT0701C / Bosch Colt as compact-router archetypes, Festool OF 1400 / Trend T11. Trim the Trend and DeWalt SKU lists; plunge/fixed/trim as router types.

k.brief: NEW: Festool Domino-type joiner; source from Festool or Wikipedia.

s.brief: Restraint: dissolve the 'Other nail guns' catch-all into Framing nailer (positive-placement/connector as a type); power source (air, gas, battery) is a type, not a kind. Trim models.

k.brief: Hand and powered riveters as types.

s.brief: Restraint: one entry per accessory family, patterns as types. Dissolve 'Other saw blades' into Saw blade. No SKU lists; at most a few market-covering makers.

k.brief: Types: twist (HSS), masonry, wood (spade, auger, brad point, Forstner), step.

depts.note: Organised kind → archetype (Stanley number, maker pattern) → version → detail.

b.m: Steel and hardening of the edge
b.v: Aogami Super > Blue #1 > Blue #2 > White #1 > White #2 (Japanese edge steels); A2, O1, PM-V11 (Western)
b.w: Leads for planes, chisels and other edged tools.

b.v: flat soles, square sides, no play
b.w: Comes right after the steel.
Premium hand tools are compared maker by maker; vintage Stanley/Record judged by type study and era.

s.brief: Archetype standard by Stanley number: Bailey bench planes Nos. 1–8 (No. 4 smoother, No. 5 jack, No. 7 jointer), Bedrock 600 series, No. 4½, low-angle jack No. 62, block planes (No. 60½, No. 9½), No. 92/93 shoulder, No. 71 router, No. 45/55 combination, No. 78 rebate, No. 151 spokeshave, No. 80 cabinet scraper. Versions: original Stanley (type study eras), Record, modern Lie-Nielsen, Veritas (bevel-up line), Clifton, Quangsheng/Luban, Woodriver, Axminster/Rider. Infill planes (Norris, Spiers, Mathieson) as archetypes under Bench plane. Keep smoothing/jack/jointer as types on Bench plane; existing models become versions. Kanna is on the Japanese shelf.

k.brief: NEW: wooden profile planes (hollows and rounds, beading).
NEW: two-handled blade for green woodwork.
NEW: card scraper and cabinet scraper (Stanley No. 80), scraper plane (No. 112).

s.brief: Tradition-led shelf: add a tradition entry for Japanese carpentry tools (daiku dōgu; Miki and Sanjo/Yoita smithing centres, Banshu Miki designated traditional craft) with steel ladder (Shirogami/Aogami). Archetypes: kanna (hira-ganna smoother, kiwa-ganna), ryoba, dozuki, kataba, kugihiki/azebiki, genno patterns (hakkaku, daruma), oire-nomi and tataki-nomi, sumitsubo, sashigane, kiridashi. Makers: Gyokucho/Razorsaw, Z-Saw (Okada), Shokunin, Tasai, Koyamaichi, Matsumura. Move Western flush-cut models (Veritas) to versions noted as Western interpretations.

k.brief: NEW: Japanese marking and utility knife.

s.brief: Archetypes: Disston D-8 and No. 7 (originator of the American handsaw), Spear & Jackson, Bahco hardpoint saw (Barracuda/ProfCut), Western dovetail saw (Lie-Nielsen, Veritas, Pax/Thomas Flinn), tenon and carcass back saws, Olson/Knew Concepts coping and fret saws, Eclipse/Bahco hacksaw frames. Japanese saws live on the Japanese shelf.

Archetypes: Marples Blue Chip/Irwin, Narex, Lie-Nielsen socket chisels, Veritas PM-V11, Ashley Iles, Robert Sorby; carving gouges with the Sheffield/Swiss sweep-number system (Pfeil Swiss Made, Two Cherries, Flexcut); turning gouges (Crown, Sorby, Hamlet); Auriou hand-stitched rasps, Grobet/Vallorbe and Nicholson files; whetstones (Shapton, Naniwa, King, Norton India, Arkansas natural stones, Japanese natural stones as a tradition link), diamond plates (DMT, Atoma), honing guide (Eclipse, Veritas Mk II) as a new kind; Tormek T-series and Work Sharp as sharpening-system archetypes.

k.brief: NEW: hand-carving chisels and gouges by sweep number.
Types: waterstone, oilstone, natural stone, diamond plate.

s.brief: Archetypes: Stanley/Millers Falls ratchet braces, Millers Falls and Stanley hand (egg-beater) drills, Yankee push drill (North Bros. No. 41/44), gimlets and bradawls. Vintage makers matter more than current ones.

k.brief: NEW: awl and gimlet for starting holes.

s.brief: Dissolve 'Other clamps' into Bar clamp (F, quick-release, parallel-jaw as types). Archetypes: Bessey KRE parallel clamp and Bessey F-clamp, Jorgensen, Irwin Quick-Grip; Record No. 52½ quick-release vice, leg vice, engineer's vice (Record No. 6, Wilton bullet vise); workbench patterns (Roubo, Nicholson/English, Moravian, Klughammer/Sjöbergs Scandinavian, Festool MFT, Black & Decker Workmate as the originator of the folding bench); Gramercy/holdfast. Merge trestle into sawhorse.

k.brief: Types: woodworking (face, tail, leg) and engineer's vice.
NEW: bench holdfast and bench dogs.

depts.note: Tier for everyday tools, variety at the enthusiast end (Knipex, Wera, PB Swiss, Snap-on, Estwing).

b.v: chrome-vanadium or better; accurate tips and jaws that do not cam out or slip
b.w: What separates good spanners, screwdrivers and pliers in independent tests.

b.v: VDE/insulated to 1000 V where electrical
b.w: Required for electrical work.

s.brief: Archetypes: Johansson/Bahco adjustable spanner (originator), Stillson pipe wrench (Ridgid), Snap-on and Britool combination spanners, Gedore, Wera Kraftform, Wiha, PB Swiss, Phillips and Pozidriv/Torx drive systems as named patterns, Allen key, Wera Joker ratcheting spanner, click-type torque wrench. Trim SKU lists. Merge basin wrench into pipe wrench as a type if thin.

Rename 'Combination and other pliers' to Combination pliers. Archetypes: Knipex Cobra and Pliers Wrench (originator), Channellock 400-series tongue-and-groove (originator), Vise-Grip 10WR locking pliers (originator, Petersen), Knipex/Klein side cutters, Lineman's pliers (Klein). New: wire stripper, crimping tool.
Restraint: trim hammer models to a few market-covering makers (Estwing, Stanley, Thor); keep pein patterns as kinds; pry bars kind-level. Japanese genno moved to the Japanese shelf.

QoL tier shelf: keep paintbrush (Purdy, Hamilton, Harris; sash/fitch as types), add the decorating kinds a householder expects with a few market-covering makers each (rollers, sprayers such as Wagner/Graco, filling knives, caulking gun, plastering trowel (Marshalltown, Refina), manual tile cutter (Rubi, Sigma)). No SKU lists.

depts.note: EDC, utility and bushcraft blades live here; kitchen knives in Kitchen, fighting and hunting knives in Weapons.

b.v: powder steels (S30V, M390, 20CV) > stainless (VG-10, 14C28N) > carbon (1095, Sandvik 12C27, Aogami)
b.w: The axis knife communities compare first.

b.v: frame lock, liner lock, back lock, slip joint, friction folder
b.w: Defines the pattern and legal carry in many countries.
Collectors compare by maker and named pattern.

s.brief: Split the flat pocket-knife list. Modern folding knife archetypes: Chris Reeve Sebenza (originator of the integral frame lock), Spyderco Delica/Endura and Paramilitary 2, Benchmade Griptilian and Bugout, Buck 110 Folding Hunter (originator of the lockback hunter), Kershaw Leek, Civivi. Traditional/regional folding knives: Opinel, Laguiole, Higonokami, Douk-Douk, Barlow, Case trapper/stockman/peanut patterns, Svord Peasant, Okapi. Swiss Army knife: Victorinox Officer's/Spartan, Huntsman, SwissChamp, Classic SD; Wenger. Multi-tool: Leatherman PST (originator), Wave, Charge, Skeletool; Gerber Multi-Plier, SOG PowerAccess, Victorinox SwissTool. Fixed-blade/bushcraft: Mora Companion and Mora Classic, Fällkniven F1, ESEE, Ka-Bar Becker. Utility knife: Stanley 99 (originator of the retractable trade knife), Olfa snap-off (originator of the snap-off blade). Add tradition entries where relevant (Laguiole/Thiers, Miki higonokami). Existing models become versions.

k.brief: NEW: regional and slip-joint patterns (Opinel, Laguiole, Higonokami, Barlow, stockman).
NEW: outdoor/utility fixed blade (Mora, Fällkniven, ESEE).

s.brief: Archetypes by pattern and maker: Gränsfors Bruk Small Forest Axe and Wildlife Hatchet, Hults Bruk, Wetterlings, Council Tool Boy's Axe, Fiskars X-series splitting axe, Estwing camper's axe; patterns (Hudson Bay, Dayton, Michigan, Kent, Scandinavian forest axe) as archetypes without makers. Splitting maul (Gränsfors, Fiskars), Kindling Cracker (originator of the kindling splitter). Folding pruning/bushcraft saw (Silky, Bahco Laplander) as new kind. Froe as new kind. Log splitter kind-level, no trade machines.

k.brief: Types: felling axe, forest axe, hatchet, splitting axe.
NEW: riving blade for splitting shakes and green wood.

depts.note: Hobby and home-workshop machines; industrial-only machines dropped.

b.v: frequent use > regular use > occasional use
b.w: Workshop machines are sorted by duty first.

b.v: cast iron over sheet steel; induction over universal motors
b.w: Compared within the same duty class.

s.brief: Archetypes: Delta Unisaw (originator of the cabinet saw), Powermatic Model 66, SawStop (flesh-sensing originator; PCS, ICS, JSS versions), Felder/Hammer combination machines (K3, A3 41, C3 31), Laguna and Record Power bandsaws, Startrite, Scheppach, Grizzly G0690-type cabinet saws, Bosch REAXX. Table-saw duty classes stay as types. Trim the long Grizzly/Felder SKU lists to versions of archetypes. New kind: combination machine (saw-spindle-planer).

k.brief: NEW: universal woodworker combining saw, spindle and planer.

s.brief: Archetypes: wood lathes (Record Power CL/Coronet, Jet 1642, Oneway, Robust, Nova), drill presses (Clarke, Record Power, Nova Voyager), desktop CNC routers (Shapeoko, X-Carve, Onefinity, Carvera), and a NEW laser cutter/engraver kind (Glowforge, xTool, Epilog hobby models). Shapeoko generations become versions.

k.brief: NEW: desktop laser cutter and engraver.

s.brief: Machinist/model-engineering archetypes: Myford ML7 and Super 7, South Bend 9/10K, Atlas, Sherline, Taig, Emco Unimat, Boxford, Hardinge; Bridgeport milling machine (originator of the turret mill), Warco, Sieg mini lathe/mill (C3, X2) and its rebrands; Grizzly and Shop Fox trimmed to versions. Blacksmithing: NEW anvil (London pattern, German/double-horn; Peter Wright, Hay-Budden, Fisher, Refflinghaus, Vaughan Brooks) and NEW forge (coal, gas). Metal bandsaw and cold saw kind-level with a few makers.

k.brief: NEW: hobby coal or gas forge.

s.brief: Restraint: trim the dust-extractor SKU list (18 models) to market-covering makers and test winners; shop vac and cyclone collector as types.

depts.note: Tier for site and trade instruments; variety for machinist and marking-out tools.

b.w: The one thing that matters for measuring and test tools.

b.v: CAT IV > CAT III > CAT II
b.w: IEC 61010 rating for meters.

s.brief: Machinist and woodworker icons: Starrett combination square (originator, No. 11/C33) and steel rules, Mitutoyo Digimatic/ABSOLUTE calipers and micrometers, TESA (Swiss) height gauges and micrometers, Brown & Sharpe, Moore & Wright, Etalon, Interapid lever indicators; Japanese kebiki as marking-gauge archetypes; Veritas wheel marking gauge, Tite-Mark; marking knives (new). Drop institutional CMM and hardness tester (done in plan).

k.brief: Sliding bevel and digital angle gauge as types.

s.brief: Restraint: trim models (Stanley, Stabila, Bosch, Leica DISTO for laser measures); rotary laser and optical level kind-level (trade).
Restraint: keep Fluke models as tier picks; other kinds kind-level or with a few market-covering makers.

b.v: higher duty cycle at rated amps
b.w: Main measured difference between welders.

b.v: multi-process > single process
b.w: Hobby buyers often pick one machine for several jobs.

s.brief: Restraint: remove repeated SIP Weldmate range from every kind; a few market-covering makers (Lincoln, Miller, ESAB, R-Tech, SIP).
Restraint: merge welding wire, rods, tungsten and brazing rod into one consumables kind with types; keep solder and flux.

k.brief: Types: MIG wire, flux-cored wire, stick electrode, TIG filler rod, tungsten electrode, brazing rod.

b.v: EN 131 Professional > EN 131 Non-Professional
b.w: EN 131 replaced the BS 2037 classes in 2018.

s.brief: Restraint: merge platform stepladder into Stepladder as a type; trim models.
Restraint: vehicle jacks and stands move to Vehicles; keep general lifting and carrying kinds, kind-level.

b.v: rated watts or CFM; dB at 7 m
b.w: Main measured differences for generators and compressors.

s.brief: Restraint: merge inverter and open-frame generators into Portable generator with types; drop repeated PREDATOR range. Trade plant (excavators, loaders, forklifts, dumpers) is out.

b.v: stacks with the owner's battery-tool brand
b.w: Modular systems (PACKOUT, TSTAK, Systainer, L-BOXX) lock only within their family.

s.brief: Restraint: modular systems stay as ranges on Portable tool box; trim others.

depts.note: Receives the PPE kinds moved in from Clothing (A1); merge any duplicates with these kinds.

b.v: EN/ANSI rating (EN 166, EN 352 SNR, EN 149 FFP1–3, EN 381 class 0–3, ANSI Z89.1)
b.w: The rating is what makes it PPE; compare comfort only within a rating.

s.brief: Archetypes: MSA V-Gard (hard-hat icon), Petzl Vertex climbing-style helmet, 3M Peltor Optime (earmuff icon) and ProTac, 3M Speedglas (originator of auto-darkening welding filters), Lincoln Viking, Miller Digital Infinity; 3M 6000/7500 half masks, 3M Aura; Uvex pheos, Bollé. Trim the Pyramex safety-glasses SKU list (16 models) to a few versions.

Restraint on chainsaw trousers (trim the 13-model list; protection class as type), merge chaps as a type if thin. Add work gloves (cut and impact ratings, EN 388), knee pads and fall-arrest harness with a few market-covering makers. Incoming A1 kinds (hi-vis clothing, workwear) merge here.
